2067.statement: Lilly gives separate examples for MARS with seventh lord or Moon in Aries/Scorpio indicating earlier desire now diminished; and Moon LADY OF SEVENTH conjoined with MARS or JUPITER (one glyph uncertain) representing an allegedly higher-status man/bishop. Mutual reception indicates attachment still present but lacking opportunity.
2067.precondition: Identify which of the Moon-as-seventh-lady Mars/Jupiter conjunction, earlier Aries/Scorpio condition, or MUTUAL RECEPTION branch applies.
2067.limit: The planet in the second joining is copy-uncertain; no Saturn is named in this original PDF349 passage, contrary to the first draft.

2069.statement: Seventh lord joined to VENUS, with reception or without aspect under the printed variants, is used by Lilly to say a woman cares not for men, but has friendship with women or speaks wantonly, while 'not naturally lewd or vitious'.
2069.precondition: The house ruler relates to VENUS alone under the given reception/trine/sextile or square-without-reception branches, continuing PDF349–350.
2069.limit: Historic speculation about friendship, speech, orientation and conduct, not a factual judgment. Mercury is NOT present in this particular printed premise.

2071.statement: Seventh lord joined to SUN signifies, by the quality of the DEMANDANT, previous attachment to a prominent person; WITH RECEPTION the person had or may have relations if desired, WITHOUT RECEPTION the person has forsaken her.
2071.precondition: Reception present versus absent between SUN and seventh ruler gives different source outcomes; questioner's quality affects social attribution.
2071.limit: The source's personal-relationship allegations have no independent verification.

2072.statement: Additional planetary contacts with SUN, especially SATURN or MERCURY, are linked by Lilly to other supposed people, while saying she is 'somewhat tardy' and 'nor is she yet amended'.
2072.precondition: Planets must behold Sun together with seventh lord under source's printed circumstances.
2072.limit: 'Tardy' may mean at fault/blameworthy in seventeenth-century use, NOT necessarily delayed; this is a qualified lexical inference, not certainty.

2074.statement: The printed 'If ones Lover or Wife hath a Sweetheart besides himself' paragraph contains DISTINCT planet-by-planet alternatives for a seventh-house occupant (not its lord): SATURN, JUPITER, VENUS, MOON, SUN and DRAGON'S HEAD, including several EXPLICIT DENIALS of an affair. Preserve those in source-review-added separate records.
2074.precondition: A planet physically occupying seventh which is NOT seventh lord, with each source-specific planetary alternative kept separate.
2074.limit: Original draft wrongly flattened these into generic class judgement and lost negations; do not infer any actual relationship.

2075.statement: In the separate 'Hath she a Lover' subsection, the seventh lord void of course indicates no admirer under the stated context, with other node/source aspects handled distinctly.
2075.precondition: Apply the separate unnumbered heading's seventh-lord and lunar signifiers; no assumption that every seventh lord VOC entails real-world absence.
2075.limit: This record belongs after the new 'Hath she a Lover' heading, not to the previous 'sweetheart besides himself' paragraph.

2076.statement: In 'Hath she a Lover', seventh lord or Moon joined with Mars may, in the special source example, indicate a respected acquaintance WITHOUT dishonourable conduct.
2076.precondition: Seventh lord/Moon–Mars relationship in this source's class of inquiries.
2076.limit: This is a protective alternative against automatic allegations; follow the separate heading.

2077.statement: The preceding 'If ones Lover or Wife...' passage says analogous judgments can be made when a woman asks concerning a man, with corresponding signifier roles and house relations changed.
2077.precondition: A woman asks about a man, and significators are reversed relative to man's inquiry.
2077.limit: This source passage belongs BEFORE the separate heading 'Hath she a Lover', despite original draft ID ordering.

2079.statement: In the late marriage-perfection section, first lord or Moon joined to seventh lord in seventh lord's dignities AND in ASCENDANT, ELEVENTH or TENTH (and HARDLY in SEVENTH) is given as possible positive sign.
2079.precondition: Marriage principal significators conjoined in seventh lord dignity AND source-listed houses, less assurance in seventh.
2079.limit: The original named placement list and 'hardly in seventh' are essential.

2080.statement: Principal signifiers beholding by sextile/trine from stated houses, WITH OR WITHOUT RECEPTION and free from prohibition, frustration, abscission or retrogradation, give marriage perfection IF THE QUERENT PLEASE—Lilly explicitly supposes freedom of will in such a question.
2080.precondition: Sextile/trine with named signifiers and appropriate house, absence of intervening obstructions, and querent's freely choosing the match.
2080.limit: The express FREE-WILL conditional prevents astrology from supplying actual consent; include 'with or without Reception' as printed.

2085.statement: When identifying a mediating third party from the translating planet, the source says a MASCULINE AND DIURNAL planet denotes a man, while a FEMININE/NOCTURNAL planet can signify a woman or a man with a feminine constitution, and vice versa.
2085.precondition: A genuine third planet carrying benevolent influence between otherwise-unconnected marriage significators.
2085.limit: Source's gendered planet categories are historical labels; prior Sun/Mars examples were not printed here.

2086.statement: Before relying on a translating planet, check if that planet or dispositor is retrograde, combust, unfortunate, cadent or in hard adverse aspect to an INFortune without reception; the phrase runs across the PDF351–352 page turn.
2086.precondition: Actual translating planet and its dispositor/aspect condition, NOT any planetary malefic elsewhere.
2086.limit: Continuation includes 'square aspect to an Infortune, without Reception' on original PDF352.

2087.statement: Where those obstacles to the transmitting planet are ABSENT, Lilly positively says the marriage will be effected and continue, especially if the intermediary is a fortune.
2087.precondition: A genuine transfer/mediator exists and no specified obstruction occurs.
2087.limit: Earlier record's separate 'may fail' was a modern inference; source explicitly states only the favourable absence-of-obstacle branch.

2094.statement: ONLY IF NONE of the earlier corroborating conception testimonies apply, Lilly says Saturn, Mars or Mercury BEHOLDING the fifth house or its lord may give 'JUST SUSPITION' a child was conceived in adultery and the mother was 'STUPRATED'.
2094.precondition: No previously listed positive conception testimonies; Saturn/Mars/Mercury BEHOLD fifth or fifth lord without an invented aspect type.
2094.limit: These are printed early-modern accusations under a source hedge, NOT genetic evidence or proof of assault or adultery. Do not silently translate 'stuprated' into a specific modern legal/medical term.

2097.statement: Seventh lord for the expelled party beholding first house or first lord 'SO PARTILLY' and with true/good aspect is said 'WITHOUT DOUBT' to indicate eventual return and restored favour.
2097.precondition: Seventh lord specifically beholds first house or ruler, with the source's particular close/true favourable aspect.
2097.limit: The author's 'without doubt' overconfidence is faithfully recorded as historical assertion, not observed reconciliation.

2098.statement: If seventh lord does NOT behold the ascendant, an OTHER unimpeded planet can mediate only if the seventh lord BEHOLDS that planet AND that planet in turn BEHOLDS the ascendant; continuation runs onto PDF353.
2098.precondition: No direct seventh-to-ascendant aspect AND specific two-step seventh→intermediary→ascendant contact; the intermediary is not impeded.
2098.limit: Mediator is not merely any favourable planet present; page-break clause is essential.

2106.statement: After recent separation from Sun's beams, Lilly attributes regret to the man who caused wife to absent herself OR had ABUSED HER, while the woman may return angry, untrusting and 'NOR WILL SHE MUCH RESPECT HER HUSBAND AFTER THAT TIME'.
2106.precondition: The source context of Venus recently separating from Sun beams, as distinct from occidental/retrograde approaching combustion.
2106.limit: The text reports possible abuse rather than demonstrating it; retained disrespect is not a clinical/safety prediction.
